Friday morning over the North Bay Interior Mountains. Conditions will
be very dry with very poor overnight humidity recoveries only
reaching 14 to 24 percent. Rapid fire spread is possible given the
combination of gusty northerly winds and very dry overnight
conditions.

Weather Watch.

* TIMING...From this evening through Friday morning.

* WINDS 20 FOOT...North winds 5 to 15 mph with gusts up to 30 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 14 to 24 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will likely spread rapidly.
Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions are
forecast during the valid watch time. These conditions could promote
the rapid spread of wildfires which could become life-threatening.
Check weather.gov/mtr for forecast updates and a possible upgrade of
this watch to a Red Flag Warning. Also consider signing up for your
city, county, or state emergency alert system.

Follow all fire restrictions. One less spark, one less wildfire.

Never leave burning debris or camp fires unattended; extinguish them
completely. Avoid using equipment or machinery that could create a
spark. Secure tow chains to avoid dragging and subsequent sparks.
Never toss cigarette butts out of your vehicle's window. Remember,
one less spark, one less flame.

moving northwest at 13 mph. A turn more to the west is expected to
occur over the next 24 hours. As 29W continues it's journey to the
Marianas, rapid intensification is possible. This would result in
increased west to southwest monsoon flow will increase. This will
allow for showers to increase in coverage any intensity, with locally
heavy rainfall likely.

higher amounts possible. If 29W can intensify a little faster than
anticipated, or if it takes a due west track, this could open door
for isolated wind gusts to 30 to 35 knots to develop. Seas currently
look to increase 1 to 3 feet, topping out near 7 feet, but again,
this could be higher if 29W tracks closer to Chuuk or strengthens
faster.

days until the developing tropical depression has passed.

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued October 14 at 2:14PM CDT until October 17 at 1:00AM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WATCH FOR PORTIONS OF SOUTHEAST TEXAS AND CENTRAL AND
SOUTHWEST LOUISIANA FRIDAY...

.With the ongoing drought conditions, we have KBDI values well into
the 700s, with 10-hour and 100-hour fuel moisture values hovering
around 25%. Subsidence behind the front will further dry out the
already dry continental air mass, leading to a significant drop in
dew points following the front. The forecast drops RH values below
30% across central Louisiana and the interior portions of
southeast Texas. Friday through Sunday look to be concerning for
fire weather. However, Saturday appears to be the most critical
day as the dry, subsided airmass becomes fully entrenched over the
highly dried out fuels. This setup is similar to the weather
conditions that sparked the Tiger Island fire in 2023, and fires
that do spark could quickly spread out of control..

The National Weather Service in Lake Charles has issued a Fire
Weather Watch for high winds and low relative humidity, which is
in effect from Friday morning through late Friday night.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 027 Vernon, Fire Weather
Zone 028 Rapides, Fire Weather Zone 029 Avoyelles, Fire
Weather Zone 030 Beauregard, Fire Weather Zone 031 Allen, Fire
Weather Zone 032 Evangeline, Fire Weather Zone 033 St. Landry,
Fire Weather Zone 044 Lafayette, Fire Weather Zone 045 Upper
St. Martin, Fire Weather Zone 141 Northern Calcasieu, Fire
Weather Zone 142 Northern Jefferson Davis, Fire Weather Zone
143 Northern Acadia, Fire Weather Zone 180 Tyler, Fire Weather
Zone 201 Hardin, Fire Weather Zone 259 Northern Jasper, Fire
Weather Zone 260 Northern Newton, Fire Weather Zone 261
Southern Jasper and Fire Weather Zone 262 Southern Newton.

* TIMING...From Friday morning through late Friday night.

* WINDS...North 15 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 35 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Up to 87.

* LIGHTNING...

* IMPACTS...Any fire that develops will catch and spread
quickly. Outdoor burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that critical fire weather conditions
are forecast to occur. Listen for later forecasts and possible
Red Flag Warnings.
